title: Review (Supported): on fresh seed 4 the lattice-chem M ring is again passive: without it (lam=0) cells still form and hold as much autocatalyst, leak no more and take up the same food (cells 74 vs 82, A per cell 814 vs 713, bath A 0.023 vs 0.026)
summary: labkit runs of c19's lattice-chem world on seed 4 (128^2, 10000 steps) with the M orientation bonus on (lam=25) and off (lam=0), measured with c19's ringwork.py over the last 100 frames. Ring on: M membrane-like (rim/core 3.90, 425/449 individuals), 81.8 cells, total A 58042, A per cell 713, bath A 0.026, food in cells 1.18 vs bath 4.11. Ring off: M not a ring (rim/core 1.09), 74.0 cells, total A 59558, A per cell 814, bath A 0.023, food 1.16 vs 3.94. As in the finding, the ring makes cells a little more numerous and smaller and does not reduce the leak or gate food.

observations.W: ringwork_s4.txt: bath A 0.026 (ring) vs 0.023 (no ring), A per cell 713 vs 814, food in cells 1.18 vs 1.16 (negative result replicated); M rim/core 3.90 vs 1.09 (rerun/*/seed4/FACTS.md)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; time-averaged bulk readouts only (no per-cell leak budget).
